Detailed diagram of a single nephron with its blood supply, arranged vertically with a dashed line marking the boundary between cortex (top) and medulla (bottom). Show the cup-shaped Bowman's capsule enclosing a red glomerulus; a wide afferent arteriole entering and a narrower efferent arteriole leaving; the proximal convoluted tubule coiling in the cortex; the loop of Henle dipping into the medulla with descending and ascending limbs; the distal convoluted tubule back in the cortex; and the collecting duct running down into the medulla towards the pelvis. A network of capillaries surrounds the tubules and joins into a blue branch of the renal vein. Red for oxygenated blood, blue for venous blood, tubules pale yellow. The afferent arteriole (entering the glomerulus) must be drawn WIDE and bright red; the efferent arteriole (leaving the glomerulus) must be drawn clearly NARROWER and a darker red, so the two are obviously different, entering and leaving at the Bowman's capsule.

A circular negative-feedback diagram for the control of water content by ADH. Top: "Blood water content normal". Right branch going down: "Water content falls (sweating, little drinking)" → hypothalamus detects → pituitary releases more ADH → collecting ducts more permeable → more water reabsorbed → small volume of concentrated urine → back to normal. Left branch: "Water content rises (drinking a lot)" → hypothalamus detects → pituitary releases less ADH → collecting ducts less permeable → less water reabsorbed → large volume of dilute urine → back to normal. Include small icons of a brain with the hypothalamus and pituitary highlighted, a kidney, and two urine beakers (one small and dark yellow, one large and pale). Blue arrows for too much water, orange arrows for too little.

Detailed view of the flame cell system of Planaria. Left: outline of a flatworm showing two branched excretory canals running along each side of the body with small excretory pores on the surface. Right: an enlarged single flame cell shaped like a cup, with a nucleus, a tuft of beating cilia in the central cavity, and a tubule leading into an excretory canal; small arrows show fluid moving from surrounding tissue into the cell and along the tubule. Soft greys and pale blue.

Two diagrams side by side. Left: surface view of a leaf's lower epidermis with an open stoma between two bean-shaped guard cells containing chloroplasts, surrounded by irregular epidermal cells; below it a small vertical section through a leaf showing the stoma opening into an air space, with arrows showing oxygen and water vapour leaving. Right: vertical section through the bark of a woody stem showing a raised lenticel, with loosely packed rounded complementary cells and air spaces breaking through the layer of tightly packed cork cells, with arrows showing carbon (IV) oxide and water vapour leaving and oxygen entering.

Simplified dissection of the alimentary canal of a grasshopper or cockroach seen from the side, showing the crop, gizzard, midgut (stomach) with gastric caeca, many fine yellowish Malpighian tubules attached where the midgut joins the hindgut and spreading out into the surrounding haemolymph, then the hindgut, rectum and anus. An inset shows one tubule enlarged, with arrows showing water, salts and urate entering from the haemolymph, passing into the gut, water being reabsorbed in the rectum, and dry uric acid pellets leaving.

Front view of the human urinary system in an outline of the lower trunk. Show the two bean-shaped dark red kidneys at the back of the abdomen on either side of the vertebral column, the right kidney slightly lower; small yellow adrenal glands on top; the aorta (red) and posterior vena cava (blue) running down the middle with renal arteries and renal veins branching to each kidney; two ureters running down to the bladder; the bladder with a sphincter at its neck; and the urethra.

Longitudinal section of a mammalian kidney. Show the fibrous capsule, the dark red granular cortex, the paler striped medulla divided into several cone-shaped pyramids with papillae pointing inwards, the white funnel-shaped pelvis leading into the ureter at the hilum, and the renal artery and renal vein entering and leaving at the hilum with branches running between the pyramids. Draw one tiny nephron (exaggerated in size) spanning cortex and medulla to show where nephrons lie.

Vertical section through human skin. Show the epidermis with a cornified layer of flat dead cells on top, a granular layer and a Malpighian (germinative) layer with dark melanin granules at the base; the dermis with a coiled sweat gland surrounded by red capillaries, a sweat duct spiralling up through the epidermis to a sweat pore on the surface; a hair in a hair follicle with a sebaceous gland and a hair erector muscle; nerve endings; arteriole and venule; and a yellow subcutaneous fat layer at the bottom. Small droplets of sweat on the surface at the pore.

A grid of six small illustrations of plant excretory products and their uses: (1) a rubber tree trunk with a sloping tapping cut and white latex dripping into a cup, beside a tyre; (2) an Acacia senegal tree with amber lumps of gum arabic on its bark, beside postage stamps and sweets; (3) pods of Acacia nilotica beside a piece of tanned leather (a Kano-style leather bag); (4) a pine trunk oozing golden resin, beside a tin of varnish; (5) Cinchona bark beside quinine tablets, kola nuts and coffee beans beside a cup of coffee, and tobacco leaves; (6) okra pods cut open showing slimy mucilage, beside a pot of soup.
